cultivation_relevance: Primary edible oilseed crop of India. Gujarat (Saurashtra region) is the largest producer in India, known for high oil content and superior bold kernels.

climate_and_soil.climate_type: Tropical and warm subtropical climate with bright sunshine
climate_and_soil.temperature_range_celsius: 25°C to 30°C optimal; sensitive to severe cold and water stagnation
climate_and_soil.annual_rainfall_mm: 500 - 750 mm well distributed during flowering and pegging
soil_types: Red sandy loam with loose light texture allowing peg penetration
climate_and_soil.drainage: Must have friable, well-aerated light soil; heavy clay soils severely restrict peg entry and make pod harvesting difficult

seasons: Summer Groundnut (February - May under assured irrigation)

planting_details.sowing_time: Kharif: June 15 to July 15 with onset of monsoon; Summer: January 15 to February 15
planting_details.seed_rate: Bunch types: 40-45 kg kernels/acre; Spreading types: 35-40 kg kernels/acre
planting_details.spacing: 30 cm x 10 cm (Bunch types) or 45 cm x 10 cm (Spreading types)

critical_stages: Pegging stage (40-50 DAS - Crucial for peg penetration!)
water_management.water_requirement_mm: 450 - 550 mm total requirement over 4 to 6 irrigations

nutrient_management.fym_manure_per_acre: 4 tonnes FYM applied during final land preparation
nutrient_management.recommended_npk_ratio: 10:20:0 kg/acre N:P2O5:K2O (Starter N + Single Super Phosphate)
micronutrients: Gypsum @ 200 kg/acre applied at pegging stage (40-45 DAS) along rows to supply essential Calcium for kernel filling and prevent 'pops' (empty pods)

harvest_and_yield.harvesting_signs: Leaves turn yellow and shed; inner shell wall develops dark brown netting; kernels separate easily from pod wall
harvest_and_yield.expected_yield_per_acre: Kharif rainfed: 8 to 14 Quintals/acre; Summer irrigated: 15 to 22 Quintals/acre
harvest_and_yield.post_harvest_storage: Dry pods in sun for 6-8 days until moisture drops to <8%; store in well-ventilated dry godowns to prevent Aspergillus flavus (aflatoxin)

pests: White Grub (Holotrichia consanguinea - destructive root pest)
